fixes.explanation: I see the thinking, but there's no city gate in this verse. Leviticus 14:3 says, “The priest is to go outside the camp to examine him…” The person had been living outside the camp (Leviticus 13:46), so that's where the priest goes. The verse sends him right out to where the person is.

At the entrance to the Tent of Meeting is right, friend! Leviticus 14:11 says the priest presents the person with the offerings “…before the LORD at the entrance to the Tent of Meeting.” Look at this guy: he's got two lambs, a ewe lamb, flour and oil, and he's standing right there in front of the LORD. I think that's a lot to carry, and I bet he's grinning anyway. Eight days ago he was outside the camp, and now he's at the Tent of Meeting.

Cleared is right, and it's smart. Leviticus 14:36 says, “The priest must order that the house be cleared before he enters it to examine the mildew…” Then comes the reason: “…so that nothing in the house will become unclean.” So the priest tells the owner to empty it out first. Now that's the kind of order I like, friend, because even my own drawer got cleared out one day, and that turned out to be the best thing that ever happened to me.
